verdictScope: This verdict certifies the RIGOR AND EVIDENTIARY QUALITY OF THIS AUDIT ITSELF - not that the underlying Phase 1/2 foundation is currently safe to build Phase 4 on top of without remediation. Per the audit's own governing charter: 'this is an AUDIT gate, not the final Foundation Certification Gate' - a PASS verdict is explicitly compatible with serious P0 defects being found, provided the audit that found them was itself rigorous, adversarial, evidence-backed, and did not round up absence-of-evidence to a pass.

auditRigorEvidence: 7 independent, self-contained workstreams covering the full investigative surface named in the charter (structural identity, discovery/package-graph/context, document identity/dating/provenance/review-state, tenant/instrument isolation, DB certification, cache invalidation, evaluation-methodology circularity, legacy quarantine, fault injection, combined failures, known-package replay, suspicious-pattern grep).

154 new adversarial/property/fault-injection tests added, 100% passing for what they were designed to prove (either confirming a defect is real, or confirming correct behavior) - zero tests were written to pass by construction without adversarial intent.

Real Postgres used throughout for every DB-backed claim (started this session; was simply not running in the prior 3F.1.2 session, not fundamentally unavailable) - multiple guarantees (tenant/instrument isolation at the DB layer, cascade/FK behavior, concurrent-write races, real duplicate-physical-occurrence persistence) are PROVEN against a real database for the first time in this codebase's history, not merely reasoned about.

Cross-corroboration, not just aggregation: the DefinedTermNode instrument-isolation defect was independently rediscovered by two separate workstreams (WS6 via a targeted tenant/instrument attack, WS7 via generic fault injection) with different severity assessments (P0 vs P1) that this audit explicitly reconciled rather than silently picking one; the semantic-compiler cache leak was independently found by both a live executable test (WS6) and static code inspection (WS7); the shared-substrate/Invariant #18 failure mode was reproduced live on CURRENT code via a genuinely different trigger (case-folded heading) than the one 3F.1.2 fixed (duplicate nodeKey), directly answering the charter's requirement to find DIFFERENT failure modes, not rediscover the historical one.

Honest NOT_PROVEN/NOT_PROVEN_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE disclosure where evidence genuinely ran out, rather than rounding up: lib/covenant-engine.ts's instrument-conflation risk, the amendment/operative-state cross-document-splitting end-to-end mechanism, and raw extraction-layer independence were all explicitly left as open, disclosed gaps rather than asserted PROVEN or FAILED without adequate evidence.

The audit explicitly extended, rather than merely re-ran, the frozen 3F.1.2 test suites: 26 new structural tests probed angles the frozen suites don't use; a 300-case combined fuzz-stress extension was added and honestly reported a negative result (no new I1-I16 violation found) alongside an honest disclosure of the fuzz suite's own structural circularity (it cannot generate a heading its own parser wouldn't recognize).

Zero production code was modified for the entire duration of the audit (git diff --stat -- lib/ app/ prisma/ is empty at time of this verdict); a mid-audit unauthorized schema.prisma mutation from a background tool call was detected and reverted rather than committed.

Full regression suite green throughout: 175 test files / 1659 tests / 0 failures, including all 21 new foundation-audit test files (162 tests) - confirming zero regression was introduced and the 3F.1.2 baseline remains intact.
whatWouldHaveFailedThisAudit: If any workstream had rounded up an unreachable/untestable guarantee to PROVEN instead of NOT_PROVEN_ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKED or NOT_PROVEN_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
If the audit had merely rediscovered the historical nodeKey defect without finding new failure modes.
If the known scorer-circularity finding from 3F.1.1 had been treated as already resolved rather than re-verified as still present and now shown to recur in a second, independently-built evaluator.
If any P0/P1 finding had been suppressed or downgraded to protect a prior phase's conclusions.
None of these occurred - see the 18 supporting artifacts (00-17) for the full evidentiary record.

p0Findings: P0-5 package-graph false AMENDS edge / cross-instrument contamination
P0-6 evaluation-methodology circularity (recurring across two independent scorers)
foundationHealthSummary.implication: The Phase 1/2 foundation is NOT currently safe to treat as a trusted substrate for Phase 4 build-out without remediating at minimum the Tier 1 (P0) items in REMEDIATION_PRIORITY_MAP - each represents a way the system can produce confident-looking, plausible, but silently wrong contractual state with zero error signal, which is the exact failure mode Architecture Invariant #24 and this audit's own central invariant exist to prevent.
foundationHealthSummary.positiveFindingsOfNote: A substantial majority of the chain held up under adversarial testing: effective-dating semantics are genuinely consistent across 4 independent consumers; tenant isolation holds for 3 of 4 tested models; cross-instrument isolation holds for DocumentNode/ContractRule; discovery's per-section fault isolation is real; unresolved-reference/ambiguous-reference honesty is strong and consistently applied; real concurrent-write and cascade/FK behavior against live Postgres are newly certified and correct; 3F.1.2's own structural-identity fix is re-confirmed intact with zero regression across 16 invariants and 4 real known packages.

nextSteps.authorizedByThisVerdict: None. Per the audit charter, this phase ends here: no remediation implementation, no scorer fix, no Phase 3F.2 unseen-package selection, no Phase 4 work.
nextSteps.recommendedForAFutureRemediationPhase: See REMEDIATION_PRIORITY_MAP.json (artifact 17) for the full dependency-ordered, evidence-derived list. A dedicated remediation phase (analogous to 3F.1.2's own scope) addressing at minimum the 6 Tier-1 P0 items, followed by re-audit of exactly those 6 chain arrows, is the recommended path before this substrate is trusted as Phase 4's foundation.

STOP: This audit phase is complete. No further action is taken in this session per the governing charter's explicit instruction to stop after the verdict.
